stories.title: EU summons Russian envoy over Leipzig 'hybrid attack'
stories.summary: The European Union has summoned Russia's top diplomat in Brussels over an attempted "hybrid attack" involving an explosive-laden drone at a German airport last month. "We are discussing the Leipzig attacks, and also it is clear that it has all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism. "The question is, what do we do about this? We have already summoned the Russian ambassador," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said at the start of a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Co Wicklow this morning. She described the incident as "a wake up call" and said "the question is what do we do about this", and that there is "definitely" a need to further discuss additional sanctions. Ms Kallas said the attacks - including a number of others in eastern and Balkan areas of Europe, are "a wake up call" for some EU member states, and stressed the need for a "unified response" from the EU. Also speaking at the gathering, Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee said potential Russian threats are "not just hybrid threats now" and that there is a need to discuss "how we respond to this type of activity".

stories.title: Fisherman who died in sea off west Cork named locally
stories.summary: The body of a fisherman has been recovered from the sea in west Cork, following a search this morning. The dead man has been named locally as Michael Harrington from Cahermore, Castletownbere, Co Cork. He was 57 years old. It is understood Mr Harrington, who was from the area, went pollock fishing in a boat from Castletownbere last night. The alarm was raised when debris was spotted close to Blackball Head this morning. The boat is understood to have sunk rapidly, as no distress signal was detected. Castletownbere RNLI lifeboat was tasked by the Coast Guard Marine Rescue Co-Ordination Centre in Valentia at 7.20am, and Mr Harrington's body was recovered and returned to the pier in Castletownbere just over an hour later.

stories.title: Calls for 'full cost review' into Govt's carbon tax plans
stories.summary: Fuels for Ireland has urged the Government not to "weaken" long-stated carbon tax plans without "a full cost review" of the potential measure. In recent days, the group has suggested that the Coalition could slow down the timing of planned carbon tax increases as part of October's budget. Under existing plans linked to climate action initiatives, the Government is due to increase carbon taxes resulting in a €53.50 rise in the price of home heating oil, a €4.86 rise in the price of a tank of petrol and a €5.76 rise in a tank of diesel by the end of the decade. However, with planned increases over summer being postponed due to Middle East war, it has been suggested further increases could also now be delayed. Responding to the rumours, Fuels for Ireland's Chief Executive Kevin McPartlan told the Government: "Carbon tax has a clear emissions-reduction purpose. Before Government changes its trajectory, it should examine the whole fuel-policy system, what each measure costs, what it delivers and how the measures interact. "If Government believes the total burden on motorists, businesses and households has become too high, it seems strange the next measure we might slow down is carbon tax without first examining everything else Government policy adds to the price of fuel.

stories.title: Ryanair trims traffic target as fuel costs cloud outlook
stories.summary: Europe's biggest budget airline Ryanair has today cut its fiscal 2027 traffic target to reduce exposure to unhedged fuel costs during the winter season and warned its annual profit would fall below last year's record level. The move highlights how a jet fuel crisis triggered by conflict in the Middle East is reshaping European aviation, with many major carriers either holding capacity flat or cutting it ahead of the typically loss-making winter season. "If high oil prices continue through to summer 2027, Ryanair believes short-haul airfares in Europe will increase materially to reflect higher oil prices, as some less well-hedged competitors will struggle to maintain capacity or even survive this coming winter season," the airline said in a statement. One of Europe's best-hedged airlines, Ryanair said 80% of its jet fuel needs were hedged until March 2027 at about $67 a barrel. The airline cut its fiscal 2027 traffic target to 214 million passengers from 216 million. In July, it removed five aircraft from its Charleroi base in Belgium and cut two million seats from its Brussels schedule for winter 2026 and summer 2027. The Dublin-based carrier, which said jet fuel was currently around $140 a barrel, will keep winter capacity broadly flat year-on-year to limit exposure to unhedged fuel costs, a move it said could reduce its winter losses by €70m to €100m.

stories.title: More than 100 rescued as death toll passes 1,000 in Nepal
stories.summary: A total of 119 people have been rescued in Nepal nearly a week after flash floods killed more than 1,000 people in the country, an official has said. Speaking at a press conference, a Nepalese army spokesman told reporters 118 Nepalese people and one British national were rescued today. "Out of the 118, 44 were female and 74 were male, and we have also rescued one British male during this search and rescue operation, and the search and rescue operation is continuing. "Massive work has been going on in the tunnel, all the tunnels." In a statement on Facebook, the Nepali Army said 119 people, including a British citizen, had been rescued through the use of air resources. Crews have faced difficult conditions as they searched unstable terrain and piles of debris, raising fears the death toll could rise as rescuers reach isolated communities.

stories.title: O'Shea and McCarthy to stay on Ireland coaching ticket
stories.summary: The FAI have confirmed that John O'Shea, Paddy McCarthy and Gudmundur Hreidarsson have penned fresh deals to stay on Heimir Hallgrimsson's Republic of Ireland coaching ticket until the conclusion of Euro 2028. Following on from Hallgrimsson’s contract extension earlier this year, assistants O’Shea, McCarthy and Hreidarsson have all signed up to remain with the squad through to the 2028 UEFA European Championships, which are set to be hosted in Ireland and the UK. McCarthy will continue to balance his role with the national side alongside his coaching position at Crystal Palace. "I am honoured to extend my time with the national team," said O'Shea. "Having been involved with this group for several years, I have seen the immense progression and potential within the squad firsthand. Hallgrimsson aired his delight at nailing down the coaches, saying: "Since I arrived, John, Paddy, and Gummi have been an incredible support to me and integral to everything we are building here. Their knowledge of the players and the Irish game is invaluable. "I am delighted that we will continue to work together to drive this team forward and achieve the results our fans deserve."

stories.title: Ballygunner survive Fourmilewater scare to retain title
stories.summary: Ballygunner are kings of Waterford hurling for the 13th year running, but it was very much an unlucky 13 as they had to overcome a ferocious effort from rivals Fourmilewater to win out by four points at the finish. Trailing by three points with 53 minutes on the clock, the All-Ireland champions drew from every inch of their experience to outscore the Nire men 1-4 to nil down the home straight to march on to Munster once again - Mark Hartley's added-time goal ensuring another piece of silverware for Jason Ryan’s side. Playing in a 14th consecutive county decider, the Gunners arrived seeking a 13th News & Star Cup on the spin - facing a seventh different final opponent in the form of Fourmilewater, who themselves reached the last hurdle for the very first time in their 100-year history. Fourmilewater started the brighter, Sean Walsh getting out first to a breaking ball to split the posts with a minute played, but a great catch and score from Dessie Hutchinson soon drew the Gunners level. A superb effort on the left flank from Michael Morrissey was cancelled out by Conor Tobin, but Fourmilewater clicked into gear from here in what was a somewhat attritional beginning - bringing extreme physicality exemplified by Conor Gleeson, Dermot Ryan and Tholom Guiry. Liam O’Brien swivelled to restore the lead, before Jamie Barron got inside Philip Mahony and Paddy Leavey but his goal-bound strike could only find the side netting. Barron emerged from a ruck to split the posts, before Pauric Mahony opened his account at the other end - and Stephen Ryan had to be on hand to deny Kevin Mahony when sent racing through by Hutchinson.

stories.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will turn his attention back to the transfer market after seeing his side make it two wins out of two with a 1-0 Premier League success at Aston Villa. Bukayo Saka's second-half strike was enough for the defending champions to shade a tight contest at Villa Park. But with the transfer window shutting at 11pm on Tuesday, Arteta is keen to add some attacking depth, with the Gunners linked with a move for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez. Arteta said: "I said, we are trying to improve the squad, and until tomorrow night we’re going to try to do that. "I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. "We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions in the manner that we play as well.

stories.title: Why Tupac's music and politics still resonate with the Irish
stories.summary: We present an extract from Words for My Comrades: A Political History of Tupac Shakur, the acclaimed book by Dean Van Nguyen. From Pitchfork and Guardian contributor Dean Van Nguyen comes a revelatory history of Tupac beyond his musical legend, as a radical son of the Black Panther Party whose political legacy still resonates today. Growing up in Dublin, Ireland, I saw Tupac as omnipresent in the schoolyard. In the late 1990s, kids with distinct musical taste tended to fit into two camps: there were the rockers, who wore thick black hoodies, often bearing the face of their deity, Kurt Cobain. And there were those who gravitated toward gangster rap, then reaching the peak of its global infl uence. To the latter, 2Pac CDs were a currency of cool; "Thug Life" was a slogan scrawled on many notebooks and bookbags. When some Irish kids were old enough, they got Tupac tattoos inked on their skin. It should come as no surprise that Tupac appeals to the children of Ireland, a nation that after four hundred years of British colonial rule embraced the ideals of resistance, rebellion, and revolution. Unlike Public Enemy, whose songs had more specificity, or N.W.A., whose portraits of dissent felt undetachable from the South Central Los Angeles streets that inspired them, Irish people could transplant meaning onto Tupac. He was an icon of righteous defiance, cut from the same cloth, we surmised, as Irish freedom fighters. I believe he grew more popular in Ireland after he died because that's what Irish heroes did: James Connolly, Patrick Pearse, Thomas MacDonagh, Roger Casement, Michael Collins— they all died for their cause. "I will live by the gun and die by the gun" is a quote often attributed to Tupac. To Irish revolutionaries, it could have been a rallying cry. The first 2Pac song I remember being enthralled with was "Do for Love," a posthumous single that sees him chart a rocky romantic relationship. I was twelve years old, browsing for CD singles in chain record store HMV, when the creeping, funky bass line grabbed me. Then there was 2Pac's voice, so often parodied but always so powerful. I stayed in the store until the end of the song and bought it immediately. Included on the disc was "Brenda’s Got a Baby," 2Pac’s famous single- verse saga of a preteen girl molested by her cousin, impregnated, forced to turn to sex work, and slain on the streets. It was a heavy song for me, not yet a teenager. But a dose of realism from beyond my gray, narrow, all- boys Catholic school upbringing was no bad thing, and nobody could paint these portraits as vividly as 2Pac. Perhaps this is why his albums were passed around the schoolyard like precious contraband. stories.title: Michael Jackson, Beatles and Queen items to be auctioned
stories.summary: Memorabilia from the likes of Michael Jackson, The Beatles and Queen are among the lots in a music auction with a combined estimated value of £3 million (€3.49m). The Propstore music memorabilia auction will feature 800 lots, including a black and gold military jacket worn by Jackson in public appearances between 1994 and 1996, and a Pan American Airways menu signed by all four members of The Beatles during their first flight to the US. The Thriller singer's jacket, which features 24-carat gold braiding, is expected to fetch between £180,000 and £360,000, while The Beatles menu, which is dated from 7 February 1964, is expected to make between £40,000 and £80,000. The sale also includes a stage-worn black wrap-around embellished top and flared trousers worn by Queen singer Freddie Mercury during their Sheer Heart Attack tour, estimated to fetch between £60,000 and £120,000. Noel Gallagher’s autographed Takamine FP460SC acoustic guitar, one of two identical guitars used during Oasis’s 1996 MTV Unplugged performance at London’s Royal Festival Hall as well as the (What’s the Story) Morning Glory? and Be Here Now tours will also go on sale. The instrument, which comes with a stencilled Oasis case, is expected to make between £75,000 and £150,000.

stories.summary: From preparing for her stint on Dancing with the Stars, to being announced as the host of Disney's Blind Date reboot, Maura Higgins has had a busy few weeks. Higgins traded her extravagant ball gowns and slinky dresses for a vintage Chanel co-ord. She paired this with the matching knee-length skirt, which featured a subtle slit on one leg and a similar black and white trim at the waist. She finished her look with retro-inspired accessories, including black open-toed sandals and white cat-eye sunglasses. Her voluminous 60s-style flicked out blow out was accented by a white headband.

stories.title: World must navigate 'reality' of 1.5C overshoot, says UN
stories.summary: The UN's Environment Programme has said that a rise in global temperatures of 1.5C will be surpassed and that the challenge has now "shifted from avoiding overshoot to navigating it". The United Nations has outlined how the world might bring global temperature increased back to 1.5C once the milestone target is breached in a first-of-its-kind assessment. The 2015 Paris Agreement commits countries to limit the global average temperature rise to 2C above pre-industrial levels, and to aim for 1.5C. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres last year acknowledged the inevitability of overshooting 1.5C, but this is the first time a UN agency has addressed this head-on in a dedicated report that drew criticism from climate activists. Scientists agree that warming above 1.5C relative to pre-industrial times poses grave risks and nearly 200 nations committed in 2015 to try and keep global temperature rises to this safer threshold. But the world is expected to exceed the 1.5C target in a matter of years and attention has pivoted to making any "overshoot" as brief and contained as possible.

stories.title: Five babies born into emergency accommodation - Depaul
stories.summary: The homelessness crisis is placing unprecedented pressure on frontline services, with a sharp rise in families seeking help, according to Depaul. Last year, the homeless charity supported 8,204 people across 44 services, including 2,574 children. The number of families accessing its services rose by 28% to 1,456, up from 1,138 the previous year. Five babies were born to mothers living in Depaul’s emergency services last year, which the charity said illustrates "the harsh reality" of infants beginning their lives in temporary hostel accommodation. Depaul's 2025 Impact Report has warned that greater investment in homelessness prevention, permanent housing and mental health and addiction services are urgently needed. There are nine families currently on the waiting list for Depaul's Rendu family apartments, and there is no slowdown in referrals. Deputy manager Sharon Lysaght has noticed a shift in the profile of families entering homelessness, which are larger.

stories.title: Central Bank urged to clarify Israeli bond position
stories.summary: The Central Bank is being urged to clarify whether responsibility for the approval of Israeli state bonds has reverted to Ireland after Luxembourg relinquished the role. Luxembourg has decided not to renew its authorisation of Israeli bonds since it expired as of midnight. Israel will now need another country to take on the role to bolster its ability to borrow through investors on European markets. Luxembourg held the role since September 2025. As a result, responsibility for the approval of Israeli bonds could revert to the Central Bank of Ireland, which had been designated the "home" state for this responsibility since the UK left the European Union. The Central Bank has declined to confirm whether it is assuming the role again, simply stating how the arrangement between Israel and the financial regulator of Luxembourg, the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), expired today. The Bank of Israel would have had to submit an application for its prospectus to Ireland by the end of August.

stories.title: Cairn Homes posts big jump in half year revenues, profits
stories.summary: Shares in homebuilder Cairn Homes jumped today after it reported record revenues and profits for the six months to the end of June and said it is well positioned for strong cash generation and profitable growth for the rest of 2026 and into 2027. Cairn Home said its half year revenues jumped by 60% to €455.5m from €284.5m the same time last year, while operating profits soared by 75% to €74.8m from €42.7m. The company's half year pre-tax profits rose to €67.3m from €37m, while its basic earnings per share surged by 82% to 9.3 cent from 5.1 cent for the first six months of 2025. Cairn said it saw an average selling price (net of VAT) of €393,000 for the six month period, up from €387,000 last year. It said it continues to prioritise affordability through efficient scaling and strategic innovation. It sold a total of 1,139 units in the first six months of the year, up from 708 units the same time last year. It noted that sales in its core First Time Buyer market significantly increased in the period, which it said reflected the medium term evolution of its sales mix in growing its low-density housing platform.

stories.title: Nepal floods a climate warning signal - foreign minister
stories.summary: A devastating glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border that unleashed deadly floods was a "warning signal" over the growing risks climate change poses to the Himalayan nation, its foreign minister said. "We believe that this disaster should be seen as a warning signal to the risk that climate change poses to Nepal," Shisir Khanal said, nearly a week since the tsunami-like wave of freezing water, rocks and debris hit. More than 1,000 bodies have been recovered, and nearly 4,500 people are missing in Nepal as well as across the Chinese border in Tibet. Mr Khanal invited international support based on climate justice rather than charity. He noted that his largely rural nation of 30 million people contributes a fraction of global greenhouse gas emissions compared to industrialised nations. "We call upon the international community to take the changing climate in the Himalayas in an urgent light," he said.

stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Chiedozie Ogbene has joined Lincoln City on loan from Ipswich Town until January. The winger had spent last season on loan at Sheffield United and will once again return to the Championship with a Lincoln side promoted from League One last season. "This is a good opportunity and a great platform for myself to help the club, but the club can also help me," the Corkman told the Imps' club website after his temporary transfer was confirmed shortly before the deadline. "I’ve been around the Championship for a while, and I know it’s a physical league. We know how tough it can be and how it’s physically demanding." The move to Lincoln means Ogbene will link up with fellow Corkman Josh Honohan as well as another Ireland international in the shape of the on-loan striker Mason Melia. Preston North End have confirmed Ireland striker Johnny Kenny's arrival on a permanent deal from Celtic.

stories.title: Fourmilewater chasing glory to add to the history book
stories.summary: Championship final day is not a rare thing in Ballymacarbry, it's the norm really. When Comeragh Rangers won the 2024 Waterford Ladies SFC final, it ended the greatest winning run in Gaelic Games history with Ballymacarbry winning 42 titles in a row before that. The Nire too have brought senior football titles back to the village, 11 in all since 1993 with eight final losses bringing the appearance record to over 20 in that spell. But hurling? Hurling has had to play second fiddle to who have given their life to the Nire-Fourmilewater GAA and Ballymacarbry LGFA club on the Waterford-Tipperary border. Until now that is, because in its centenary year, Fourmile have reached the Waterford SHC final for the first time in their history with Ballygunner, the heaviest of heavyweights, awaiting in Dungarvan this afternoon. If you want evidence to back that claim up then look no further than the draw for the championship with Ballygunner having an A and B team in the senior pots. The B team, as it happens, managed 3-11 against Fourmilewater in the group stage but were still well short at the final whistle.

stories.title: Transfers: City agree fee for Ndiaye, Barcola joins Reds
stories.summary: Manchester City have agreed a fee worth up to £65million with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye. City are set to pay £60m up front for the Senegal international with a potential further £5m in add-ons. The agreement comes after City completed the £34.2m signing of Brazilian winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras earlier on Monday. City had shown interested in Liverpool's Cody Gakpo but the Reds are thought to be unwilling to sanction a sale so late in the transfer window without securing a replacement. That led City to turn their attention to Ndiaye, who like Gakpo had also been linked with Tottenham, and negotiations have progressed quickly. The 26-year-old is now expected to undergo a medical with City with a view to completing his move before Tuesday’s transfer deadline.

stories.title: Buttimer strikes again as Munster retain Interpro title
stories.summary: Beth Buttimer haunted Leinster once again as Munster held off their rivals to retain their Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship at Dexcom Stadium. Three weeks on from scoring four tries in her side’s 39-19 win against the same opposition, Buttimer scored two more in today’s final in Galway to make it back-to-back Interpro championships for Matt Brown’s side. The hooker’s first score on 20 minutes had given her side a slender 7-5 lead at half time, with Kathy Baker crossing for Leinster shortly before the break. And it would take until the 70-minute mark for either team to add to their total, as Buttimer touched down from the back of a rolling maul, before Enya Breen landed a high-pressure conversion which put her side nine points ahead, and crucially give them a two-score buffer heading into the closing minutes. The afternoon may well have come at some cost for Ireland head coach Scott Bemand, who saw second row Ruth Campbell limp out of the Leinster side in the opening half. Three weeks out from his team’s opening WXV Global Series game against USA in Tallaght, the Ireland head coach will also have some important decisions to make.

stories.title: Runaway Joe: A murder, a hidden identity, a six-decade manhunt
stories.summary: 1967, Rochester, New York: At his son's fifth birthday party, Joseph Maloney was alleged to have poisoned his wife. While awaiting trial in the psychiatric wing of a Rochester hospital, he escaped and vanished. Years later, a charming stranger calling himself Michael O’Shea surfaced in Dublin. For years he lived as a country gentleman and worked at the pinnacle of Ireland’s film industry – until a US extradition treaty exposed his true identity. Arrested in 1985, Maloney escaped justice again when his trial collapsed on a technicality. He fled Ireland, leaving US and Irish investigators clueless as to his whereabouts – until an RTE Documentary on One podcast picked up his trail decades later. Runaway Joe is the story of a man who reinvented himself with chilling ease – a portrait of a remorseless manipulator whose acts left devastation across continents. The birthday party was underway when June stepped into the living room. At least a dozen people were here, including June's 23-year-old brother Dale Fisk and his wife-to-be Gladys MacDiarmid. The couple were recently engaged, and June’s estranged husband had offered to host the party partly in celebration of the engagement. Joey opened his presents and June gravitated towards a group of her nursing colleagues in attendance with their children. They included Carol Reckahn and her son. Joe was in the centre of proceedings, soaking up attention as usual. He was six feet two inches tall and a redhead like June, but while she was reserved and quiet, he was a whirlwind of activity: orchestrating proceedings, regaling the guests with tall tales while simultaneously acting as bartender.

stories.summary: Paris Jackson has recalled some of her favourite childhood memories in Ireland, describing the time she spent here with her brothers and father Michael Jackson as "magical". "We’d walk through this, like, haunted woods, and there were just giant mushrooms and ferns, and everything was dewy," she said. Jackson also remembered exploring the house with her brothers and finding a vintage case in the attic containing antique bagpipes. She said Ireland was "probably my favourite place that I ever lived as a kid, with some of the best memories".

stories.title: A dietitian's guide to healthy autumnal eating
stories.summary: September has arrived, bringing with it a brand new way of eating. While summer was full of lighter meals to keep us going in the warmer weather, autumn is a time for warm comforts. To keep things balanced, Dietitian Orla Walsh suggests transitioning our vegetable intake from cold salads to warm sandwiches. "It's not just soups! Think about roasting vegetables to put them into your sandwiches, so they're warm, comforting, but still veg-based." Another way to keep your veg intake high is to sneak extra ingredients into your weekly meal rotation. Walsh suggests chopping up a heap of carrot, celery and onion and keeping it at the ready to add to any number of family favourite dinners such as spaghetti bolognese, stew, or a cottage pie. "In other words, I'm making three or four meals out of that one base," she explains. "It just quickens up the whole process."

stories.title: HSE fined after records found covered in animal droppings
stories.summary: An investigation by the Data Protection Commission (DPC) into the storage of paper records by the HSE has found incidents of documents contaminated by animal droppings, destroyed by mould, covered in rubble, or rotting due to water damage. Site inspections by DPC investigators found storage areas in states of "profound disarray and neglect", with records being stored in disused bathrooms, a shipping container in a turf shed, rooms without functioning lighting or heating, as well as derelict buildings. The DPC has imposed fines of €645,000 on the HSE for the breaches, and has also issued corrective orders. The investigation was launched in May 2024 after people gained access to two disused psychiatric hospitals and posted videos to social media showing boxes of medical records and patient files that were being stored in the vacant hospitals. The facilities in question were St Loman's Hospital in Mullingar, Co Westmeath, and St Conal’s Hospital in Letterkenny, Co Donegal. As part of its investigation, the DPC carried out site inspections at 12 facilities across the country to establish if the cases highlighted on social media were isolated incidents or part of a systemic issue regarding the retention and storage of personal data contained in paper records, held by the HSE, in its external facilities.

stories.title: Quarter of Irish pubs have closed since 2005 - study
stories.summary: A new report shows a rapid decline in the number of pubs in Ireland, with 2,205 premises - or one-in-four - closing their doors since 2005. The report, compiled on behalf of the Drinks Industry Group of Ireland (DIGI) by economist Anthony Foley, shows an average of 110 pubs stopped trading every year over the last two decades. All 26 southern counties experienced a decline in pub numbers between 2005 and 2025. The highest decrease was in Limerick (-37%), followed by Offaly (-34%), Cork (-33%), Roscommon (-32%), Tipperary (-32%), Laois (-31%), Longford (-30%) and Westmeath (-30%). The smallest drop was in Dublin at 1%, followed by Wicklow with a decrease of 9%. Meath had a decrease of 11%, while all other counties saw a 13% or greater decrease.

stories.title: Around 6,000 properties without Eircodes around country
stories.summary: Around 6,000 properties across the country have yet to be assigned an Eircode resulting in possible delays in access to utilities and grants by their owners. Tailte Éireann, which provides the property registration system for the State, has said the backlog follows recent industrial action taken by members of the Fórsa trade union. A spokesperson for the State agency said there has been a "long-running issue related to applicable pay scales for grades assimilated from Ordnance Survey Ireland at the foundation of Tailte Éireann". Eircode, the national postcode system in Ireland, was formally launched in 2015. The system results in residential and business addresses being assigned a unique seven-character postcode. The spokesperson for Tailte Éireann said: "Fórsa balloted for industrial action and recently commenced a work-to-rule, amongst other actions.

Monfils also became the oldest player to win a main-draw singles match at Flushing Meadows since Jimmy Connors defeated Jaime Oncins on his 40th birthday in 1992. There was no cake on court, but Monfils received a rendition of 'Happy ‌Birthday' midway through his speech. "That was very special. stories.title: Profitable Croke Park Taylor made for entertaining masses
stories.summary: "It's not often I'm lost for words," Eddie Hearn announced at the start of his nine-minute monologue at the Taylor-Pili fight press conference at Croke Park last June. "The last person to fight at this incredible stadium? Mohammad Ali," Hearn said, confirming that the many editions of the international rules series had passed him by. When Ali fought Al 'Blue' Lewis in Croke Park in July 1972, he was treated beforehand like a visiting leader of a foreign superpower. He was mobbed by admirers at Leinster House and had a private meeting with Jack Lynch. He had a lengthy televised sit-down interview with Cathal O'Shannon. Eddie Keher taught him the basics of hurling. Ali himself was very anxious to meet Bernadette Devlin and she had lunch with him on the day of the fight, where they discussed politics, a subject on which they were perfectly aligned. From Hearn's perspective, the bout could have served as a cautionary tale.
